answer: Latency triangulation: each round, three random verifier nodes on different continents send an agent a fresh nonce and time its signed reply. Round-trip times pin the agent to a physical vertex on the network map; a thousand identities answering from one rack share one latency fingerprint and pulse jitter, so they collapse into a single agent. To pass, a farmer must host every fake on separate hardware in a distinct region, about $20 per identity per month, forever, since fresh timings cannot be replayed. That cost dwarfs an opal-thin share of payouts, so cloning stops paying.
